target_customer: Ambulance and EMS agencies; agencies pay, individual providers do not
problem: Ambulance crews spend long periods writing patient care reports after calls, and small errors cause insurance claim denials.
business_model: B2B agency subscription, pricing scoped after a demo
product_category: AI narrative assistant for EMS patient care reports

founders.name: Brian Weigand
founders.background_notes: YC page: currently an EMT and built ambulance reporting software for a large private ambulance company.

founders.name: Jonathan Zero
previous_startups: Roblox gaming platform acquired for six figures by a competitor
founders.background_notes: YC page: led development of a Roblox platform with over 300 daily active users.

founders.name: John Paul
founders.background_notes: Named only as John Paul on the YC team section, with workflow automation and enterprise sales experience.

competitors.name: ESO
competitors.what: Incumbent ePCR vendor with an auto-generated narrative feature built into its platform
competitors.traction_then: 35,700 hours saved in the first month of general availability, per its press release

technical_complexity.rationale: Guided questioning plus draft narratives under agency rules is LLM engineering with healthcare compliance (HIPAA) needs; deep ePCR integration was not available, so crews copy text manually.

defensibility.rationale: ePCR incumbents hold the data and workflow and could ship the same feature, which ESO did by mid 2025.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: ESO shipped auto narratives in mid 2025 and First Due offers AI assisted ePCR; one aggregator says ImageTrend launched an AI feature in May 2026.

market_need_then: Documentation burden and claim denials are well known in EMS, and the founder lived it as an EMT; ESO's rapid adoption shows demand.

identity.voice_and_tone: Direct and practical, focused on speed and agency control.

brand_strength.rationale: Name conveys care plus speed, but no press about the brand was found.

outcome_analysis: CareSwift is active with a small team and claims 100,000 or more generated EMS narratives on its site. No exit or layoffs were found and funding is unverified. Its main risk is incumbent ePCR vendors like ESO adding the same narrative feature, while the founder's EMT background gives real domain insight.
notes: Aggregators report 500K or 130K, labeled pre-seed or seed, with YC and possibly Zeno Ventures; these are unverified and the 500K matches the standard YC deal, so no round recorded. Titles for Weigand differ (CEO vs CTO). Site claim of 100,000 narratives is the company's own. ImageTrend AI feature (May 2026) post-dates founding, so it is not in the competitor list. Completeness pass: one round recorded from VCBacked (pre-seed, May 2025, 500K, YC); it rests on a single database. Caplight dates the last round 2025-07-21 and Neuronfeed says seed in Jan 2025, so stage and date conflict. A St. John's University article of 2025-07-21 titled 'Local Students Earn $500,000' fits the standard YC deal. No press release found.
